source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-192577:If holding down swap hands key over output of furnace, item occasionally is invisible until updated
source_meta._title: Shift clicking banners out of loom causes ghost items

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 in a single-player world. Use Creative mode as a deterministic way to obtain a loom and exactly 16 identical banners. Keyboard and mouse instructions assume default controls; use the equivalent bound controls if they have been changed.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected version Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2, not the fix version 21w10a or a later release.
Have a single-player Creative-mode world available. No particular seed, biome, structure, or coordinates are required by the report.
The player inventory must have at least two empty slots: one for a stack of 16 identical blank banners and one for a loom.
Use one banner type throughout the procedure. This plan uses blank White Banners; do not mix colors, patterns, custom names, or other banner data.
Use a mouse and keyboard, or controls capable of performing the inventory actions equivalent to right-click and Shift+left-click.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the 1.15.2 installation, select Singleplayer, and create or load a Creative-mode world. For a new world, select Create New World, change Game Mode to Creative, and select Create New World again.
steps.exact_input: Launcher installation: 1.15.2; Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a fully loaded world in Creative mode, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory and select the Search Items tab so the item-search field is available.
steps.exact_input: Press E; click the Search Items tab
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open and a text search field is visible.

steps.action: Search for a blank White Banner. Left-click the White Banner result to pick up its full stack of 16, then left-click an empty hotbar or player-inventory slot to deposit the stack. Do not use a patterned, renamed, or differently colored banner.
steps.exact_input: white banner
steps.success_cue: One player-inventory or hotbar slot contains exactly 16 White Banners in a single stack.

steps.action: Replace the inventory search text with "loom". Obtain one Loom from the search result and place it into a different empty hotbar slot. If the cursor picks up more than one loom, retain at least one loom in the hotbar; the additional loom count does not affect the banner-stack condition.
steps.exact_input: loom
steps.success_cue: A Loom is present in the hotbar, and the separate stack of exactly 16 White Banners remains intact.

steps.action: Close the inventory, select the hotbar slot containing the Loom, aim at the top surface of a solid block within reach, and place the loom.
steps.exact_input: Press E; select the Loom hotbar slot; right-click a solid block surface
steps.success_cue: A loom block is placed in the world directly within the player's reach.

steps.action: Open the placed loom by aiming at it and using it.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the loom
steps.success_cue: The loom interface is open. Its banner input slot is visible above the player's inventory, and the stack of 16 White Banners is visible in the lower player-inventory area.

steps.action: In the player-inventory section of the open loom interface, right-click the stack of 16 White Banners once. This splits the even stack in half: 8 banners remain in the original inventory slot and 8 banners attach to the mouse cursor.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the 16 White Banner stack once
steps.success_cue: The original player-inventory slot shows 8 White Banners, and the cursor holds the other 8 White Banners.

steps.action: Move the cursor to the loom's banner input slot—the loom slot intended to accept a banner—and left-click once to deposit all 8 cursor-held White Banners into it. Leave the other stack of 8 identical White Banners in its existing player-inventory slot. Do not add dye or a banner pattern.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the loom banner input slot
steps.success_cue: The loom banner input slot contains 8 White Banners, the cursor is empty, and a separate stack of 8 identical White Banners remains in the player inventory. The inventory stack has exactly 8 spaces available, equal to the 8 banners in the loom.

steps.action: With the loom interface still open, hold the inventory-transfer modifier and left-click the stack of 8 White Banners in the loom's banner input slot exactly once. Release the inputs after the click, and do not click any resulting inventory slot before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.exact_input: Hold Left Shift and left-click the 8 White Banners in the loom banner input slot once
steps.success_cue: The Shift+left-click transfer action has just been performed, the loom interface remains open, and no additional inventory interaction has occurred.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just Shift+left-clicked the 8 White Banners out of the loom's banner input slot while a separate incomplete stack of 8 identical White Banners was present in the player inventory. The loom interface is still open and no subsequent click has updated the inventory; begin observation immediately.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a required game mode, world seed, coordinates, or whether the test must use single-player or a dedicated server. This plan uses a single-player Creative-mode world solely to make item acquisition deterministic.
The report requires banners of the same type but does not specify a color or pattern. This plan uses blank White Banners as the simplest identical banner type.

The report allows any counts satisfying its stack-capacity condition. This plan uses 8 banners in the loom and 8 in the inventory because the inventory stack then has exactly enough capacity to accept the loom stack and complete the maximum banner stack of 16.

The report does not specify how long the extra inventory state remains available for inspection. The handoff therefore occurs immediately after the triggering Shift+left-click and before any further inventory action.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MC-267433:Shift double-clicking while holding the same item on your cursor doesn't transfer items
source_meta._title: Single shift-clicking on items while holding the same item with the cursor stacks the items

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 23w51b in a single-player Creative-mode world, using keyboard-and-mouse inventory controls. Use an ordinary Chest and one full stack of a single block type; this plan uses 64 Stone as the deterministic example.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected snapshot 23w51b rather than the fix version 24w03a.
Use a world in which the player can place and open an ordinary Chest. A newly created Creative-mode world is used here only to simplify item acquisition; the report does not specify a game mode.
Ensure the player inventory has at least one empty slot available as a potential quick-move destination.
Use the configured Sneak/quick-move modifier when instructed; its default keyboard binding is Left Shift.
Perform only a single Shift+left-click at the trigger step. Do not double-click.

steps.action: From the Minecraft Launcher, start Minecraft Java Edition using the installation/profile for snapshot 23w51b. Do not use 24w03a, which is listed as the fix version.
steps.exact_input: Select installation 23w51b, then click Play.
steps.success_cue: The main-menu version text identifies the running game as snapshot 23w51b.

steps.action: Create or load a single-player world in Creative mode. After entering the world, wait until nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded world and can fly or access the Creative inventory.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory and select the Search Items tab, identified by the compass icon.
steps.exact_input: Press E, then click the compass-shaped Search Items tab.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open and its item-search field is visible.

steps.action: Obtain an ordinary Chest item. Click the search field, enter "chest", left-click the result named Chest, and left-click an empty hotbar slot such as slot 1 to place the chest stack there. Do not choose a Trapped Chest or Ender Chest.
steps.exact_input: Type: chest; left-click Chest; left-click hotbar slot 1.
steps.success_cue: An ordinary Chest item stack is in hotbar slot 1 and the mouse cursor is not carrying an item.

steps.action: Replace the search text with "stone", pick the ordinary block named Stone, and place its full 64-item stack into a different empty hotbar slot such as slot 2.
steps.exact_input: Click the search field; press Ctrl+A; type: stone; left-click Stone; left-click hotbar slot 2.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 2 contains exactly 64 Stone, the chest remains in another hotbar slot, and the mouse cursor is empty.

steps.action: Close the Creative inventory and select the hotbar slot containing the ordinary Chest.
steps.exact_input: Press E, then press 1 if the Chest was placed in hotbar slot 1.
steps.success_cue: The world view is visible and the Chest item is selected in the active hotbar slot.

steps.action: Aim at the top surface of a nearby solid ground block and place one ordinary Chest.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the target ground surface.
steps.success_cue: A normal wooden Chest block is present directly in front of or near the player.

steps.action: Aim at the placed Chest and open it.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the Chest.
steps.success_cue: The Chest interface is open, showing the chest storage grid above the player's inventory and hotbar.

steps.action: Move the full stack of 64 Stone from the player's hotbar into an empty slot in the chest storage grid. First left-click the 64-Stone hotbar stack to attach it to the cursor, then left-click an empty chest slot to deposit the entire stack.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the 64 Stone in the hotbar, then left-click an empty slot in the chest's upper storage grid.
steps.success_cue: One chest slot contains 64 Stone, the original player hotbar slot is empty, and the cursor carries no item.

steps.action: Left-click the 64-Stone stack in the chest once to pick up the entire stack with the cursor. Keep the pointer positioned over that now-empty chest slot.
steps.exact_input: Single left-click on the 64-Stone chest slot.
steps.success_cue: The original chest slot is empty and the cursor is carrying 64 Stone.

steps.action: Without moving to another slot, right-click the same empty chest slot exactly three separate times. Each right-click deposits one Stone while retaining the remainder on the cursor.
steps.exact_input: Right-click; right-click; right-click.
steps.success_cue: The chest slot under the pointer contains exactly 3 Stone while the cursor still carries the remaining 61 Stone.

steps.action: Keep the cursor over the 3-Stone stack and press and hold the configured Sneak/quick-move modifier, which is Left Shift by default.
steps.exact_input: Press and hold Left Shift.
steps.success_cue: Left Shift remains held while the chest interface is open, the pointer is over the 3-Stone chest stack, and 61 Stone remain attached to the cursor.

steps.action: While continuing to hold Left Shift and while the cursor still carries the same Stone item type, left-click the 3-Stone chest stack exactly once. Do not double-click or perform any further inventory action before handing control to the observation subsystem. Left Shift may be released after the single click has been registered.
steps.exact_input: While holding Left Shift: single left-click once; then release Left Shift.
steps.success_cue: One Shift+left-click input has just been issued on the 3-Stone chest stack while the cursor was carrying 61 Stone, and the chest interface remains open for immediate inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The chest interface remains open immediately after the player has single Shift+left-clicked the 3-Stone chest stack while holding 61 Stone of the same type on the cursor. No additional clicks or inventory actions have been performed; begin observation now.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus multiplayer, a world seed, or a required game mode. This plan uses a new single-player Creative-mode world as the simplest deterministic setup.
The report says only to use a stack of blocks and does not identify a block type. This plan uses ordinary Stone; the test condition is that both stacks contain the same item type.
The report says to place "a few" items back into the chest without specifying a count. This plan uses exactly three, leaving 61 Stone on the cursor and 3 Stone in the chest slot.

Creative inventory normally supplies a full stack of the selected item. If the chosen UI configuration supplies a different quantity, ensure the chest initially receives exactly 64 of one block type before continuing.
